question: Should OpenClaw add dynamic ack reaction selection, and if so should the contract be a configured emoji array, deterministic/random strategy, rule-based selector, or model-driven pre-ack hook?
rationale: This changes a shipped cross-channel config/API surface and ack reactions are emitted before normal reply generation, so code inspection cannot safely choose the user-facing semantics or compatibility boundary.

options.title: Approve a shared selector contract
options.body: Add a backward-compatible shared `ackReaction`/`ackReactions` or selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

options.title: Keep single-value ack reactions
options.body: Defer this direction and keep variability to manual `message(action=react)` calls plus existing lifecycle status reactions.

options.title: Design a plugin/channel hook first
options.body: Add or extend a typed plugin/channel seam before core config grows if maintainers want extension-owned pre-ack selection behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve a shared selector contract
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible shared `ackReaction`/`ackReactions` or selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest shared ack-helper history and prior review context for this exact issue.
